newsitem.title: USA: Spending on public transit worthwhile - study.
newsitem.headline: Spending on public transit worthwhile - study.

text.p: Spending on public transportation gives taxpayers a four-to-one return on their money, according to a study released Tuesday.
The report released by The Campaign for Efficient Passenger Transportation showed that taxpayers reap a return of $62 billion each year from their $15 billion investment in public transportation.

The returns primarily are a result of effective mobility and reduced congestion costs, the study showed. Mobility value due to public transport was estimated worth $33.7 billion each year and averted congestion costs $19 billion annually.
Safety benefits, parking cost savings and averted roadway costs also contribute to a return on the investment from public transportation, the study said.
Advocates for public transportation funding welcomed the report at a time when Congress is re-writing the federal transportation law, the Intermodal Surface Transportation Efficiency Act.

"This report demonstrates that when it comes to investing in mass transit, the taxpayers get a lot of bang for their buck," Senator Frank Lautenberg, a New Jersey Democrat, said in a statement. "If we want America to be on the right track in the 21st Century, we've got to invest in public transportation."

The study showed that without public transportation, the New York City area would see almost a 50 percent surge in traffic. Motorists in the Chicago, Washington, Boston and San Francisco areas would see traffic increase about 20 percent.
